subject: Orion Health — DPF & DPA Annex: technical clarifications
messages:

Subject: Clarifications on DPF evidence and DPA annex

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the quick walkthrough yesterday. As we prepare our security packet for the board and procurement committee, there are a few items where we need explicit statements or example evidence to close the review: 

1) Key management — can you confirm whether customer keys are supported (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments and whether Redwood holds any key material for Hosted API? We need a short paragraph we can include in the packet.
2) Cross-border processing — we need a concise explanation of how requests originating in the EU are handled when routed to US-hosted inference, including whether IPs/IDs are exported and how pseudonymization/aggregation is applied.
3) Subprocessor list — please provide the current list and indicate whether any subprocessors are located outside the EU.
4) Logs & retention — sample log schema and retention windows for request-level logs (trace, request id, token counts).
5) DPA Annex redline — our legal team will provide markups; can you confirm who on your side will own negotiation for the security/tech annex?

If you can send draft language and attachments by EOD Wednesday (US time) that would help keep our timeline.

Appreciate it —
Sara
Sara Liu
Procurement Lead, Orion Health Systems

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@orionhealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on DPF evidence and DPA annex

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. I’ve put together short, board-ready statements for each ask and attached a DPF evidence matrix plus our current DPA annex draft for review. High-level answers below; see attachments for detail.

1) Key management
- Hosted API: Redwood manages encryption at rest and in-transit keys; customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private (bring-your-own-KMS/HSM). We do not retain customer-managed key material when BYOK is enabled; keys remain in the customer KMS.

2) Cross-border processing (EU -> US)
- Routing policy: requests from EU customers can be pinned to region (EU-only) when using Private or Dedicated. For Hosted customers that leverage our global serving layer, we provide Data Processing Framework (DPF) controls: request metadata is minimized, identifiers are pseudonymized where possible, and we maintain contractual safeguards (DPA annex + SCC/DPF measures).

3) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessor list is attached (subprocessor_list.csv). We flag subprocessors outside EU in the first column. We follow standard notice-and-consent flows and offer review periods on request.

4) Logs & retention
- Attached is a sample log schema in the DPF matrix. Typical retention windows: request traces and token-level metrics retained 90 days by default for Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention per contract. Logs are pseudonymized (no raw customer PII) in operational views.

5) DPA Annex
- Kimberly will be the point person for annex negotiation (cc’d). For technical clarifications, David can field engineering/ops questions.

I’ve attached: redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf (draft), dpf_evidence_matrix_orion.xlsx (sample artifacts), subprocessor_list.csv. Let us know any redline turnarounds and we’ll scope responses.

Best,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks Evelyn, that was helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our security team: 

A) For Hosted API customers that don’t BYOK, can you confirm whether model KV cache or any request-level cached prefixes are stored in a way that would allow re-identification of an EU data subject if processed in the US? We need an explicit statement for the board packet.
B) For Dedicated/Private with BYOK, is remote attestation or HSM-backed sealing supported for model artifacts and KV cache?
C) Legal wants to hand their annex markups to Kimberly by Thursday COB; is that feasible?

Also attaching the procurement checklist — if you can drop the redline to Kimberly, that’ll speed things up.

Sara

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara.liu@orionhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications on DPF evidence and DPA annex — technical follow-up

Hi Sara — quick technical clarifications to A/B above: 

A) KV cache and re-identification risk (Hosted)
- Our serving runtime splits prefix/KV caches by tenancy and encrypts caches at rest. For Hosted customers without BYOK, caches are stored encrypted using Redwood-managed keys and are segregated per tenant. We do not index or persist raw prompt inputs in secondary analytics tables that could be used for subject re-identification; operational logs are pseudonymized and access-controlled. Based on our design, the risk of reconstructing a single EU data subject from cached prefixes is assessed as very low; for board language: 

"Redwood segregates and encrypts runtime caches by tenant and does not persist raw prompt inputs outside of ephemeral execution contexts. Operational logs are pseudonymized and access is restricted to authorized personnel under contract."

B) BYOK + HSM/attestation (Dedicated/Private)
- For Dedicated and Private, BYOK customers can use their own cloud KMS or an on-prem HSM. We support sealing model artifacts and cache encryption with HSM-backed keys and can provide attestation reports for on-prem packages. Remote attestation for managed Dedicated pools is on our roadmap; current offering includes HSM-backed key usage and documented key lifecycle controls.

If it helps, I can provide a short SRE-runbook paragraph describing key rotation and emergency key revocation steps.

—David
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

• For any requests that must remain EU-only, we recommend Private or Dedicated pinned to EU regions to provide a technical guarantee rather than relying on contractual-only measures.

Looking forward to your markup.
